classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the supplied altitude bisects the isosceles triangle's base, use Pythagoras to find the height, then calculate area without prematurely rounding.

content.prompt: Find the perpendicular height, $h$, of this isosceles triangle, then calculate the area to 2 d.p.

spec.description: Upright isosceles triangle with external double-ended dimension arrows labelling both sloping sides 8 cm and the horizontal base 6 cm. A dashed altitude labelled h meets the base at a right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: Equal sides 8 cm; base 6 cm; altitude bisects the base. Geometry uses vertices (-3,0), (3,0), and (0,sqrt(55)).
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied givens remain visible; no calculated height or area appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height bisects the base, so each half is $3\,\text{cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=8^2-3^2\\h&=\sqrt{55}\,\text{cm}\\A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{6\times\sqrt{55}}{2}\\A&=3\sqrt{55}\,\text{cm}^2\\A&\approx22.25\,\text{cm}^2\quad\text{(2 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$
